steps.say: Most congenital heart block starts with the mother, not the child. Maternal anti Ro SSA and anti La SSB autoantibodies cross the placenta and inflame the fetal conduction system into fibrosis. By the time the slow rhythm is noticed, the atrioventricular node is often replaced by scar.
steps.tx: Congenital complete **atrioventricular block** follows transplacental passage of **maternal Ro/SSA antibodies** and anti La/SSB. Antibody mediated inflammation scars the **AV node and His bundle** during mid gestation. The atria keep sinus rhythm while the ventricles escape slowly on their own, and the two never synchronise again.

steps.say: The risk concentrates in lupus and Sjogren mothers. Neonatal heart block complicates about 2 percent of first pregnancies, then jumps to 15 to 20 percent in later pregnancies once a child has been affected. Every subsequent fetus is watched with serial rhythm surveillance through the vulnerable weeks.
steps.tx: Maternal The **maternal lupus association** means **systemic lupus erythematosus** or **Sjogren syndrome** carries about **2 percent** risk in the **first pregnancy**, rising to **15-20%** in **subsequent pregnancies**. Risk peaks between 16 and 26 weeks when the conduction system is most exposed. Fetal echocardiographic rhythm checks through this window catch progression early.

steps.say: The fetal heart rate tells how urgent things are. A sustained ventricular rate below 50 to 55 beats per minute, or any hydrops fetalis, signals a high risk of intrauterine demise. Such fetuses need a tertiary centre, timed delivery, and a pacing plan ready at birth.
steps.tx: Breaching the **fetal bradycardia threshold**, a sustained **ventricular rate below 50-55 bpm** or **hydrops fetalis**, indicates high risk of **intrauterine demise**. Poor output swells liver, skin, and cavities as the failing heart falls behind. These thresholds trigger referral, **steroid consideration**, early delivery planning, and a neonatal pacing team on standby.

nodes.label: Ventricular rate under 50 to 55 or hydrops seen

steps.say: Steroids can halt the march but cannot resurrect dead conduction. Fluorinated corticosteroids such as dexamethasone at 4 milligrams per day may arrest progression in incomplete or second degree block. Once complete block with fibrosis is established, no drug restores conduction.
steps.tx: **In utero maternal steroid therapy** with **fluorinated corticosteroids (dexamethasone 4 mg/day)** may arrest progression in **incomplete or second degree** heart block but do **not reverse complete block**. Steroids calm active inflammation and effusions while conduction still survives. Maternal diabetes, hypertension, and growth restriction limit blind use, so therapy stays selective and monitored.

steps.say: The newborn ECG is unmistakable once seen. Dissociated P waves march through a slow wide ventricular escape rhythm that ignores the atria entirely. Twelve lead confirmation separates true congenital block from hidden SVT, hyperkalaemia mimics, and monitor artefact.
steps.tx: Congenital block shows **dissociated P waves** with a slow **wide QRS ventricular escape** rhythm on the **twelve lead ECG**. Atrial rate stays normal while ventricular rate idles near 40 to 55. The tracing in this lesson is the reference image every trainee should memorise, because machine readings often mislabel it as sinus bradycardia.

vis.alt: Twelve lead ECG with rhythm strip shows dissociated P waves and slow wide ventricular escape.
vis.caption: ECG shows complete dissociation with ventricular escape rhythm. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.say: Not every slow baby needs wires immediately, but the thresholds are clear. Class I indications for permanent pacing in congenital complete block are symptomatic bradycardia, a ventricular escape under 50 to 55 beats per minute, or a wide QRS escape. Heart failure, syncope, or QT prolongation all point the same way.
steps.tx: The **infant permanent pacing indications** (Class I) in congenital complete block are **symptomatic bradycardia**, **ventricular escape under 50-55 bpm**, or **wide QRS** escape rhythm. Exercise intolerance, heart failure, pauses, and ventricular ectopy strengthen the case. Asymptomatic infants with narrow faster escapes may wait under close Holter watch, but most eventually qualify.

steps.say: Small babies need the leads outside the veins. Epicardial pacing systems are placed in infants under 10 to 15 kilograms to avoid venous occlusion and leads that tether as the child grows. The generator sits in the abdomen and the leads screw onto the heart surface.
steps.tx: **Epicardial pacing in infants** uses **epicardial pacing systems** placed under **10-15 kg** to avoid **venous occlusion** and lead stretching with **growth**. Transvenous leads in tiny veins thrombose and run short within years. Abdominal generators with surface leads trade a bigger operation now for decades of reliable capture later.

vis.alt: A heart cutaway shows a leadless pacemaker capsule anchored in the right ventricle with its femoral delivery route.
vis.caption: Leadless pacemaker anchored in the right ventricle after femoral delivery. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.say: Block also follows the knife, and patience sorts most of it. Postoperative complete atrioventricular block that resolves within 7 to 10 days can simply be watched with temporary wires in place. Persistence beyond 7 to 10 days mandates permanent pacemaker implantation before the child leaves hospital.
steps.tx: **Postoperative surgical AV block** means **postoperative complete AV block** resolving within **7-10 days** can be monitored with temporary epicardial wires. Persistence beyond **7-10 days** mandates **permanent pacemaker implantation before discharge**, because late recovery is rare and discharge with block risks sudden death. VSD, AV canal, and Fallot repairs carry the highest surgical block rates.

steps.say: Older children earn pacing on the treadmill, not just on the ECG. Failure of the ventricular rate to rise appropriately during exercise testing defines chronotropic incompetence in congenital block. A child who cannot lift the rate with effort will struggle at play and sport, so a blunted exercise response indicates pacing.
steps.tx: **Chronotropic incompetence** means failure of the **ventricular rate to increase appropriately** during **exercise testing** in older children with congenital block. A flat rate response caps cardiac output exactly when demand peaks. Documented incompetence with symptoms or poor exercise capacity **indicates pacing**, and rate responsive modes restore the missing acceleration.
